feeds.title: The Black Expat
feeds.description: The Black Expat is a multimedia platform focused on Black identity and international living. Since 2016, we have created and curated content to reflect the diverse, inclusive experiences of both the aspiring and savvy Black expatriate.

feeds.title: That Bella Life Blog
feeds.description: For Black Expats living abroad or considering relocation abroad. We are two retired California Baby Boomers who set out on a journey of self discovery, adventure and a new life outside of the United States. We believe you must bring your whole self to the table if you want to thrive in today's crazy world; your personality, your sense of humor, and most importantly, your heart.

feeds.title: My Parisian Life
feeds.description: I'm Yanique Francis. I've been living in Paris for 15 years . You will discover fun, local, and authentic Paris with me. No tourists traps!

feeds.title: Candace Abroad
feeds.description: Heya! It's Candace. Travel blogger and expat helping you explore London and live your best life, wherever that takes you. Sharing weekly doses of travel inspiration with practical information on all things London, travel, and life abroad I hope my blog inspires you to explore the beauty of London and beyond!

feeds.title: Expat Life Ghana Blog
feeds.description: Over here at Expat Life Ghana, we are always pumping out fresh content to help you navigate your visit or your big move to West Africa. Get all the information you need to plan your move, settle into life in Ghana, or plan your most epic vacation yet.

feeds.title: Blaxit Global Blog
feeds.description: Blaxit Global provides information, inspiration, and empowerment for members of the African diaspora who want to pursue a new life abroad. Our community consists primarily of Black Americans interested in leaving the United States to remove themselves from systemic racism, discrimination, oppression, and other indignities.

feeds.title: Black Women in Europe Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to the multi-award winning Black Women in Europe Blog! This is a place to celebrate the ordinary and extraordinary lives of women of the African Diaspora living in Europe.

feeds.title: An Unstoppable Journey
feeds.description: Traveling the world and running it, too. That is what the travel blog An Unstoppable Journey is all about. Monique, an American expat, and mom of 2 who has lived in The Netherlands for more than 20 years is on a quest to 'run the world', and to date, has run over 40 full and half marathons in 34 countries across six continents.

feeds.title: The British Berliner Blog
feeds.description: The British Berliner is a lifestyle expat travel blog about culture, history, travels around the world, Europe, and being British in Berlin. It will focus on a British girl from Manchester living in Berlin, her promotion of British-German life, culture, history, literature, theatre, style, Europe, travels around the world, what she does in normal everyday life and where she goes.

feeds.title: Oneika the Traveller Blog
feeds.description: As an Emmy Award-winning lifestyle correspondent for NBC New York and host of Travel Channel's Big City, Little Budget and One Bag and You're Out, Oneika inspires us to live our best lives at home and abroad. A bona fide travel junkie keen to share her insights from around the world, Oneika also appears regularly as a travel expert on CTV Canada's Your Morning and The Social. Her adventures have taken her to over 120 countries on 6 continents.

feeds.title: Black Girl In Budapest
feeds.description: Community for travelers and expats in Budapest. Wife, Mom, USA Expat who loves to explore. Tips on things to do in the city, events & being black in Budapest.

feeds.title: My American Meltingpot
feeds.description: Lori L. Tharps is a journalist and author whose work lands at the intersection of race and popular culture. A public intellectual, Tharps strives to use her words to broaden the conversation about race in America; to challenge racial stereotypes; to dismantle white supremacy; and to celebrate ethnic and cultural diversity whenever possible.
